summary: A robust resonant two-qubit gate scheme for rare-earth-ion systems uses asymmetric parallel excitation and pulse engineering to achieve decoupled qubit control, avoiding susceptibility to frequency errors and AC Stark shifts. Simulations demonstrate gate fidelities exceeding 99% within a 170 kHz detuning tolerance with off-resonant excitation below 0.2%.
motivation: Rare-earth-ion qubits suffer from spectral inhomogeneity and weak dipole-dipole coupling, making existing detuned pulse schemes fragile against frequency errors and AC Stark shifts.
method: The authors propose a resonant gate scheme employing asymmetric parallel excitation combined with pulse engineering to achieve decoupled control of the two qubits in the dipole-dipole interacting system.
result: Simulations on rare-earth-ion ensemble qubits achieve gate fidelities exceeding 99% over a 170 kHz detuning range while maintaining off-resonant excitation below 0.2%.
